stem: What procedure may be necessary if a patient develops abdominal compartment syndrome due to high intra-abdominal pressure ($>15-20$ mmHg)?

options.text: Laparotomy and temporary extrusion of the bowel into a bag
Insertion of a chest tube for fluid drainage
Immediate escharotomy of the lower limbs
Aggressive fluid boluses to maintain perfusion

explanation: This drastic measure is required to relieve the life-threatening pressure in the abdominal compartment.
rationale: Consider a surgical opening of the abdomen to create more space for the internal organs.

optionExplanations.A: This drastic measure is required to relieve the life-threatening pressure in the abdominal compartment.
optionExplanations.B: A chest tube addresses pleural issues, but abdominal compartment syndrome specifically requires intervention in the abdominal wall.
optionExplanations.C: Limb escharotomy relieves pressure in the arms or legs, but will not resolve high intra-abdominal pressure.
optionExplanations.D: While fluid is needed for shock, adding more fluid can actually worsen compartment syndrome by increasing edema.

source.hint: Consider a surgical opening of the abdomen to create more space for the internal organs.
